SYN-PUB-08743 covers link-budget prediction and SYN-PUB-08741 covers compact antenna design; neither record covers adaptive spreading-factor control or packet-recovery algorithms.

The ReachRate project must deliver improvements within 14 months, and the fixed-price municipal contracts limit budget for gateway infrastructure overhaul (C008-CH1, C008/news/2024-09-03/Elekron Sistemi Receives Provincial Innovation Fund Grant for LoRaWAN Signal Research).

why.text: The challenge identifies inconsistent welding practice across shifts as the suspected root cause of spatter defects on thin sheet-metal panels, and sets a target of under 1.5% rework rate.
Simić co-authored publications on low-spatter MIG/MAG welding parameter optimisation for thin mild-steel sheet using response surface methodology and design of experiments.
Simić co-authored a publication on shielding gas composition effects on spatter and bead geometry in MIG welding of thin sheet.

Simić co-authored a publication on pre-weld surface contamination effects on arc stability and weld quality, and co-authored a publication and led a project on SPC implementation for powder coating pre-treatment lines.

problem.text: Using design-of-experiments and response surface methodology, characterise the MIG welding parameter window and surface-cleanliness conditions that minimise spatter on thin mild-steel enclosure panels, and implement SPC control charts to hold those conditions consistently across both shifts, targeting a rework rate below 1.5%.

risks.text: The publications cover thin mild-steel sheet; enclosure-panel alloys or gauge ranges outside that scope may not be directly covered.
The DOE and SPC work addresses process parameters and pre-treatment; it does not cover automated in-line spatter detection for panels that still exhibit defects after optimisation.

why.text: The challenge states that manual inspection catches only about half of defective parts before coating, and that the company is open to vision-based approaches with no production stoppages.
Stojanović co-authored a publication on few-shot defect detection on reflective and challenging material surfaces using prototypical networks and reflection-aware preprocessing.
Stojanović co-authored a publication on unsupervised anomaly detection for multi-product assembly line environments without collecting defect examples in advance.
As academic partner in the VISIONQC project, Stojanović leads algorithm development and validation to translate research outputs into production-ready inspection components for SMEs.

problem.text: Develop and deploy a machine-vision inspection module — using few-shot or one-class anomaly detection on metallic surfaces — at the pre-coating stage of Elekron Sistemi's fabrication line to flag spatter-defective panels before powder coating, without requiring long production stoppages.

risks.text: SYN-PUB-06396 validates methods with two industrial partners producing metal stampings and injection-moulded plastic components; the challenge requires inspection of welded sheet-steel panels before powder coating, a surface type not covered by those validations.

SYN-PRJ-0011 describes development and validation of inspection components for SMEs; C008-CH2 states the workshop runs two shifts and cannot afford production stoppages, a deployment constraint the project record does not address.

why.text: The challenge traces two field failures to race conditions in the interrupt layer of a bare-metal C firmware codebase and requires systematic detection without a rewrite (C008-CH4).

Paunović co-authored work on static analysis for data-race detection in interrupt-driven C firmware using lock-set analysis and GCC plugins (SYN-PUB-10581), and co-authored separate work on dynamic shadow-memory race detection in interrupt-driven firmware (SYN-PUB-10238).
Paunović co-authored work on formal verification of interrupt-driven firmware using model checking in SPIN and Promela (SYN-PUB-10588, SYN-PUB-10586, SYN-PUB-10583).

Paunović co-authored work on incremental model extraction and continuous formal verification of evolving embedded firmware integrated into build systems (SYN-PUB-10590); the company has a Jenkins CI pipeline already in place (C008).

Paunović collaborated with a company working on automotive and industrial control products during SAFE-MIGRATE, providing refactoring support for a production motor-controller firmware codebase (SYN-PRJ-0383).

problem.text: Apply lock-set static analysis and model checking of interrupt-driven firmware to identify race conditions in the RTU interrupt layer, bound interrupt latency on ARM Cortex-M, and integrate incremental formal verification into the existing CI pipeline — without a full firmware rewrite (C008-CH4, C008, SYN-PUB-10581, SYN-PUB-10238, SYN-PUB-10588, SYN-PUB-10582, SYN-PUB-10590).

risks.text: The publications cover interrupt-driven firmware race detection; coverage of flash-write timing hazards specifically as a race-condition class is not stated in those records (SYN-PUB-10581, SYN-PUB-10238).
The SAFE-MIGRATE collaboration covered a motor-controller codebase; whether that work scaled to a 340,000-line codebase comparable to the RTU firmware is not stated (SYN-PRJ-0383).

why.text: The challenge requires systematic race-condition detection in a large legacy bare-metal C codebase integrated into CI, without a firmware rewrite (C008-CH4).

Kostić co-authored work on stack boundedness verification in interrupt-driven programs using CBMC (SYN-PUB-04582), and co-authored work on bounded model checking of timed automata specifications (UPPAAL models translated to SMT-LIB) for automotive body-control modules (SYN-PUB-04579).
Kostić co-authored work on counterexample generation techniques in software model checking, including CEGAR-based refinement and concurrent program analysis (SYN-PUB-04581).
Kostić co-authored work on incremental verification of patched firmware by reusing SMT proofs and change-impact analysis (SYN-PUB-04586).

Kostić worked with a Serbian automation equipment manufacturer on a firmware component under a research cooperation agreement, integrating formal verification artefacts into IEC 61508 safety cases (SYN-PUB-04585).

problem.text: Use bounded model checking and counterexample-guided refinement to detect concurrency hazards in the RTU interrupt layer, and apply incremental verification to re-check firmware after each patch — keeping the production firmware intact (C008-CH4, SYN-PUB-04582, SYN-PUB-04581, SYN-PUB-04586).

risks.text: The bounded model checking publications cover stack boundedness and general interrupt-driven programs; explicit treatment of interrupt-during-flash-write race conditions as a specific hazard class is not stated in those records (SYN-PUB-04582, SYN-PUB-04579).
The static analysis work covers Frama-C and MISRA-C compliance; whether these tools scale to a 340,000-line codebase for data-race detection specifically is not stated in the records (SYN-PUB-04580).

The company states the budget is limited (C008-CH4); SMT-based bounded model checking on a 340,000-line codebase may require significant computational resources and iteration time that the records do not address.

why.text: OsiguroMi's core difficulty is unstable loss curves from fewer than 200 historical events, and the company's actuarial team cannot complete this work on its own (C004-CH3).
Szabó's expertise covers extreme-value theory and generalised Pareto distribution modelling for heavy-tailed risk data specifically in small samples (SYN-PUB-09112, SYN-PUB-09113, SYN-PUB-09110).

Szabó's work includes Bayesian hierarchical models for credibility-adjusted tail quantile estimation in heterogeneous risk groups, and collective risk modelling with posterior predictive distributions for aggregate loss from sparse historical data (SYN-PUB-09116, SYN-PUB-09111).

Szabó led the statistical methodology work package of CATTOOL, an open decision-support toolkit for underwriting and reserving departments implementing GPD-based tail models and Bayesian updating routines, piloted with two regional insurers in Hungary and Serbia (SYN-PRJ-0117).
Szabó is open to contract research on tail risk quantification and extreme-loss modelling and consulting for insurance companies on Bayesian reserving (R0842).

problem.text: Szabó and OsiguroMi would apply generalised Pareto distribution modelling and Bayesian hierarchical credibility estimation to the company's database of under 200 festival-weather events, to produce stable loss curves with calibrated confidence intervals for parametric precipitation-trigger pricing across locations in the region (C004-CH3), using methods from SYN-PUB-09110, SYN-PUB-09113, SYN-PUB-09111, and SYN-PUB-09116.

risks.text: The publications cover flood, agricultural, and motor insurance loss data (SYN-PUB-06563, SYN-PUB-09116, SYN-PUB-08138); none is recorded as covering precipitation-triggered parametric event-cancellation insurance specifically.
Results must be applicable within six to nine months, which is the company's stated condition for joint projects (C004).

why.text: OsiguroMi requires a methodology applicable to different locations in the region despite sparse event history (C004-CH3), and has access to RHMZS meteorological data (C004).
Arsić's work includes regional frequency analysis using L-moments and Wasserstein barycenters to reduce estimation uncertainty for rare multivariate quantiles at ungauged locations (SYN-PUB-07511).

Arsić co-authored work on peaks-over-threshold modelling and threshold selection diagnostics for bivariate extremes, and on max-stable processes fitted by pairwise composite likelihood for spatial risk assessment of extreme precipitation (SYN-PUB-07506, SYN-PUB-03207).
Arsić carried out a six-month consulting engagement developing copula-based aggregate loss models for weather-related claims portfolios in the Adriatic–Pannonian region (R0664).

problem.text: Arsić and OsiguroMi would apply regional frequency analysis and peaks-over-threshold copula methods to the company's festival-weather event database and RHMZS precipitation records, to reduce estimation uncertainty for rare precipitation quantiles across locations in the region and support stable parametric pricing (C004-CH3, C004), using methods from SYN-PUB-07511, SYN-PUB-07506, SYN-PUB-03207.

risks.text: Arsić's publications cover environmental extremes including precipitation and discharge (SYN-PUB-07512, SYN-PUB-07511, SYN-PUB-07507); the profile records contract research on statistical risk modelling for insurance or reinsurance but not actuarial loss-curve construction or parametric insurance pricing as a primary focus (R0664).
Results must be applicable within six to nine months, on the condition set by the company (C004).

why.text: OsiguroMi states that weather stations are sometimes 30 km from the insured plot and that the company is uncertain how to reliably combine RHMZS data, private agrometeorological network data, and satellite soil-moisture indices into a single trigger that corrects payouts (C004-CH1).

Đukić has published on geostatistical interpolation of sparse climate station networks using ordinary kriging, kriging with external drift, regression-kriging, and co-kriging (SYN-PUB-08102, SYN-PUB-08098, SYN-PUB-08096, SYN-PUB-08093).
Đukić has published on spatial interpolation of precipitation in complex terrain using kriging variants, including wet-day indicator kriging for binary precipitation mapping (SYN-PUB-08096).

problem.text: Đukić and OsiguroMi would develop a spatially accurate rainfall estimate per plot for Vojvodina and Bačka by applying kriging variants and regression-kriging to the company's ~140-point mixed gauge network, augmented by satellite soil-moisture indices, to produce per-plot rainfall estimates that can serve as corrected triggers without replacing the contracted threshold (C004-CH1, SYN-PUB-08102, SYN-PUB-08096, SYN-PUB-08098).

risks.text: Đukić's publications cover spatial interpolation of precipitation and agroclimatic indices (SYN-PUB-08102, SYN-PUB-08098, SYN-PUB-08096, SYN-PUB-08093, SYN-PUB-08100, SYN-PUB-08099); none of them cover parametric insurance design or basis risk assessment.
The company requires results applicable within six to nine months (C004).

why.text: OsiguroMi's audit identified the specific error types — duplicate entries, incorrect timestamps, and flights technically cancelled but displayed as delayed — as the source of 3.1% of false payouts, and the company holds a log of all previous API calls and payouts totalling around 340,000 entries (C004-CH2).

Mirjana Malešević co-authored work on consistency validation across multiple API sources using event reconciliation, field-level comparison, and conflict detection for distributed systems (SYN-PUB-06616).

Mirjana Malešević co-authored work on design patterns for embedding data quality checks into streaming pipelines, covering inline validators, quality-aware processors, and batch reconciliation (SYN-PUB-06619).
Mirjana Malešević led the APIGUARD project, which integrated data quality monitoring into API gateway infrastructure for small and medium enterprises (SYN-PRJ-0115).

problem.text: Mirjana Malešević and OsiguroMi would design and embed an inline API-stream credibility checker — combining field-level consistency rules and unsupervised anomaly scoring (SYN-PUB-06616, SYN-PUB-06618) — into the existing claims pipeline, using the historical log of all previous API calls and payouts, to flag duplicate entries, incorrect timestamps, and flights technically cancelled but displayed as delayed before the payout trigger fires (C004-CH2, SYN-PUB-06616, SYN-PUB-06618, SYN-PUB-06619).

risks.text: The DAQSTREAM project conducted pilot deployments with industry partners in logistics and retail sectors (SYN-PRJ-0114).
Results must be applicable within six to nine months (C004).

why.text: OsiguroMi's existing rules engine produces false alarms that block legitimate payouts, and a credibility-assessment method is needed before the payout trigger activates, so the user receives a notification before leaving the airport (C004-CH2).

Olivera Rakić co-authored work on semi-supervised anomaly detection using constrained one-class SVM on benchmark datasets including bearing signals and ECG records (SYN-PUB-00960), and on self-training with uncertainty filtering for semi-supervised anomaly detection in high-dimensional process data (SYN-PUB-00962).
Olivera Rakić co-authored work on concept drift detection in streaming data using adaptive windowing and documented detection latency for sudden and gradual drift (SYN-PUB-00961).

problem.text: Olivera Rakić and OsiguroMi would apply semi-supervised anomaly detection and concept-drift monitoring (SYN-PUB-00960, SYN-PUB-00961) to the historical payout log to assess the credibility of incoming data before the payout trigger activates, so the user receives a notification before leaving the airport (C004-CH2).

risks.text: The records cover anomaly detection in industrial sensor and telemetry streams (SYN-PUB-00963, SYN-PRJ-0118, SYN-PRJ-0119); API event validation, field-level consistency checking, and structural error detection in REST responses are not covered.
The profile states limited capacity for new long-term commitments before mid-2025 (R0071).

noMatches.reason: Not a research problem: The company needs practical regulatory documentation work and technical file amendments under EU MDR 2017/745: drafting responses to a notified body's 23 queries, updating IEC 62304 records, and strengthening traceability between risk management and software safety classification—a consultancy or regulatory affairs specialist task, not research.
Not a research problem: A corporate legal and financing matter requiring shareholder agreement renegotiation and cap table restructuring, not a technical or scientific problem.

Not a research problem: The challenge is grant administration and process management; it requires building a reusable internal workflow or arranging administrative partnership, not solving a technical or scientific problem.

Not a research problem: This is financial modelling, business case preparation, and bank financing work; research cannot solve a three-year cash-flow and sensitivity analysis requirement for a loan application.
Not a research problem: A methodology and business process problem: quantifying financial risk in euros is a domain expertise and policy issue, not a scientific or technical research question.
Not a research problem: Public procurement compliance, notarial certification, and local-content clause interpretation are legal and administrative matters, not technical or scientific research.

Not a research problem: This is a regulatory and legal problem: obtaining FMA insurance intermediary licensing in Austria. The procedure requires documentation certified by the original representative who has resigned. Research cannot solve regulatory compliance paperwork or licensing procedures.
